videos.title: Rails Tutorial | How to build a blog with Rails 5 and Bootstrap 4 - Part 1
videos.description:
In this Rails tutorial, we'll build a blogging application completely from scratch. Check out https://www.techmaker.tv for tons of more content like this.

HEADS UP: In your Gemfile, you will need to change:

gem 'bootstrap' 

to:

gem 'bootstrap', '4.0.0.alpha3'



Download the code from the Github repo:

https://github.com/StephenFiser/FrogBlog

In this episode, we go over setting up a basic project with Ruby on Rails 5 and Bootstrap 4. We talk about how to build nice looking URLs for your blog posts using the FriendlyId gem.

We also go over how to pass variables between the layout and the view using yield and provide.

Finally, we discuss instance variables and ERB tags.

videos.title: Create User Account Roles In Devise | Ruby On Rails 7 Tutorial
videos.description:
This tutorial will show you how to add users, moderators, and admins to your Ruby on Rails 7 application. We do this by creating a role integer that we then convert to a readable enum.

This enum may then be used in a similar manner to how we used the admin boolean in my previous Ruby on Rails 6 Devise tutorial. I decided to create this updated Ruby on Rails 7 Devise tutorial to cover a different way to create devise user admins and moderators, as the previous one was less polished.

videos.title: Beginner's Guide to Installing Ruby on Rails - by Typecraft
videos.description:
Curious about Ruby on Rails? Want to install it and try it out yourself?  Start here.

In this video, @typecraft_dev will walk you through setting up your full Rails development environment on macOS, step by step. Whether you’re new to programming or just new to Rails, this is the perfect place to start.

What's covered:
[00:00] What is Rails?
[01:59] Installing Xcode Command Line Tools – essential compilers and utilities
[02:58] Installing Homebrew, the powerful macOS package manager
[06:06] Installing system libraries like OpenSSL, libyaml, GMP, and Rust
[07:11] Using Mise, a Ruby version manager
[09:03] Installing Ruby 3.4.2
[09:50] Brief intro to Ruby Gems and why Rails is just one of many
[10:33] Installing Rails 8.0.2, the latest version of the framework at the time of this recording
[11:05] Choosing your database: sticking with SQLite3 for simplicity, but we cover PostgreSQL/MySQL options too
[11:57] Creating and running your first Rails app
[12:54] Seeing the Rails welcome page live at localhost:3000

Even if you're on Linux or Windows, you’ll learn the key concepts that apply to any OS, so watch and learn.

👇 Helpful links (as mentioned in the video):
Official Rails Installation Guide: https://guides.rubyonrails.org/install_ruby_on_rails.html
Homebrew: https://brew.sh/
Mise Version Manager: https://mise.jdx.dev/

👉 Subscribe to be notified when 'Rails New', the next series lands. In it, we’ll explore how Rails helps you go from idea to MVP ridiculously fast. Perfect for beginners curious about Rails!

**

Learn more about Rails at: https://rubyonrails.org/

Subtitles (Japanese, Spanish, and Brazilian Portuguese) thanks to Happy Scribe, a transcription service built on Rails. https://www.happyscribe.com/
